title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference: October 21 | Week 7 vs. Denver Broncos
headline: RB Jeremiyah Love sat out Wednesday's practice and won't return until he feels 100%, with Bam Knight's strong game not changing that; Budda Baker and Jedrick Wills are out with illness.
summary: LaFleur opened with the injury report: Jeremiyah Love, along with two other players whose names were garbled in the captions, did not practice Wednesday. An illness going around the building also sidelined Budda Baker and Jedrick Wills for the day. Everyone is day to day and will be re-evaluated Thursday. Love is feeling better, but LaFleur said he won't put him on the field until he is fully healthy, and Bam Knight's strong performance doesn't change that. LaFleur praised Darius Robinson's growth and work ethic and said he still has a long way to go. On offense, LaFleur said the team hasn't been clean in its pre-snap operation and wants to improve its run-game execution and YAC. He took responsibility for the red-zone struggles, saying he needs to give better clarity and play design but doesn't want to overcorrect. He said Arizona had mixed results against man coverage, with some separation that didn't turn into plays. He called Denver's defense smart, well coached, old-school in its coverages and a big challenge.

injuries.detail: Did not practice Wednesday. He is feeling better, but LaFleur won't play him until he feels 100%. The coach did not say whether he will play Sunday.
Out of Wednesday's practice with an illness going around the team. He will be re-evaluated Thursday, day to day.

signals.note: Love's availability is uncertain, so check Thursday and Friday practice reports before setting lineups.

signals.claim: Knight's strong game will not factor into the timeline for Love's return.
signals.note: Knight stays the fill-in RB while Love is out, but the coach gave no sign his role will grow if Love returns.
signals.quote: now the what bam did has nothing to do with us.

signals.note: Robinson is earning strong praise from the coach and could become a bigger piece of the defense, though IDP impact is unspecified.

topics.detail: LaFleur said red-zone play-calling starts with him and that he needs to provide better clarity and play design. He said the team has been decent in the red zone this year apart from the New York game and last week, and doesn't want to overcorrect.

He said the pre-snap operation is the area that still needs the most improvement, and that the run game has grown in variation and execution but has more to fix. He also wants better YAC from drop steps and transitions.
He said the offense had chances to call better plays and chances where receivers separated but the team still didn't finish the play. He said there is room to improve.

LaFleur said he doesn't regret burning a timeout near the end of the Detroit game to keep Detroit six yards from the goal line instead of three. He said Brissett's pre-snap issue was somewhat unlucky and that he'll sometimes make wrong decisions and learn from them.
He called Denver smart, well coached and unapologetic about an old-school approach to coverage that has been strong for several years, saying 'we got our hands full.'
An illness is going around the building, including coaches. It forced a schedule adjustment, but LaFleur said it was not a big disruption.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Media Availability | Wednesday, October 21st | Press Conference
headline: AJ Terrell, Kendal Daniels, C.J. Henderson and Divine Deablo are all working back from injury with no game status given, while Stefanski promises to keep finding ways to get Bijan Robinson the ball after a poor offensive showing against Chicago.
summary: Stefanski opened by saying injured players will be handled day by day. Some will practice and some won't, and he wouldn't rule anyone in or out for Sunday's home game against the undefeated 49ers. AJ Terrell is set to practice, Kendal Daniels is doing much better and will practice (it is not a concussion), and C.J. Henderson and Divine Deablo are improving but their week is unclear. Jake Matthews is healthy. Stefanski took responsibility for the offense's failure against Chicago, saying the team didn't play or coach well and never got into its offense. He talked up Bijan Robinson as a player who affects both the run and pass game and said the staff will keep looking for ways to use him. He said the offensive line has plenty of room to improve, that protecting Michael Penix Jr. depends on scheme, technique and getting the ball out as well as blocking, and that the offense has been inconsistent. He praised Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey and the 49ers' offensive line, and said the defense improved its run fits after the Baltimore game. Charles Snowden was added from the practice squad and Zachariah Branch's special teams role is unchanged.

title: Jesse Minter on Lamar Jackson's Health, Defensive Growth
headline: Lamar Jackson got limited work with the team on Wednesday but his status for Sunday vs. Cincinnati remains day-to-day; Cam Jurgens is cleared from protocol and expected to start at center.
summary: Minter opened by saying the team is trying to rebound after a tough loss and prepare for a divisional home game against the Bengals. He said Lamar Jackson got a little limited work in with the team on Wednesday, but his availability is day-to-day and he would not detail progress, only saying Jackson will play when he is ready from both sides (healthy enough and the team feels it's right). He praised Jackson's mental handling of the injury and said no one wants to play more than him. Minter explained that Cleveland loaded the box, played tight man coverage and took away outside zone runs in the second half, and he expects other teams to copy it, acknowledging the offense couldn't sustain drives. Cam Jurgens is through the concussion protocol, was out of the non-contact jersey, and Minter expects him to help the offensive line right away and potentially make his first start for Baltimore. On defense he cited progress against the run, physicality and chemistry, with third down still a focus, and said confidence and conviction are what's holding the unit back. He expressed continued confidence in kicker Tyler Loop after the team brought back Jake Moody as a backup, and said the statuses of two players (referred to as Coney and Randall) are a mix of health and roster decisions.

injuries.detail: Got limited work with the team on Wednesday; day-to-day, Minter wouldn't share specifics on progress and said he'll play when healthy enough.
Cleared concussion protocol over the weekend, out of the non-contact jersey, expected to be ready to help this week.

signals.claim: Jackson's availability for Sunday against Cincinnati is undecided and will be determined day by day.
signals.note: He's practicing in a limited capacity, which is progress, but there's no commitment to him playing, so monitor Thursday/Friday reports.
signals.quote: it's a day by day thing

signals.claim: Jurgens is cleared from protocol and is expected to make his first start for Baltimore on Sunday.
signals.note: A veteran center stabilizing the interior line could help the run game and pass protection for Baltimore's skill players.
signals.quote: I expect him to actually really lift that area for us.

signals.claim: Loop remains the starting kicker despite Jake Moody being brought back as a backup.
signals.note: Kicker job looks safe for now, though competition on the roster adds slight risk if he struggles.
signals.quote: I still got a ton of confidence in Tyler

Minter sees improvement against the run, physicality, third down and chemistry, but says the unit still needs more confidence and conviction to play aggressively and adjust in real time.

Minter praised Zac Taylor's offense and Cincinnati's receivers and line, calling the matchup a chess match of team defense, and highlighted Dexter Lawrence as an impactful interior defender against the run and as a pass rusher.
Two players referred to as Coney and Randall have come a long way from their issues, and the team is balancing health with roster timing, calling it a little of both.

title: Dave Canales on Panthers run defense: 'It’s not being talked about enough'
headline: Jaelan Phillips (re-aggravated hamstring) is likely out Sunday vs. Tampa Bay, Thomas Incoom is out week to week with a calf injury, and Nick Hampton is in line for OLB snaps.
summary: Canales said the Panthers held a lower-intensity 'Work Wednesday' walkthrough-style practice with some veteran rest days, and he is excited about the division game against Tampa Bay. Jaelan Phillips re-hurt the same hamstring, and Canales said he fairly anticipates Phillips will not play this week. The team will test Phillips and look at the Thursday night game the following week, but it is being cautious because the MRI findings call for more intensive treatment. Thomas Incoom has a significant calf injury and is week to week, which hurts special teams depth and his OLB snaps. Nick Hampton will get an opportunity at OLB, with other players to follow if needed. Canales praised the run defense, which held back-to-back opponents under 50 rushing yards, crediting scheme tweaks, fundamentals, and the secondary's run fits, plus Derrick Brown's return (31 snaps vs. Philly). He also praised Tommy Tremble's two touchdowns and toughness, spoke warmly of Bryce Young's growth in his 50th start, and said he is encouraged by Robert Hunt's settling in despite two penalties. On the offensive line, Brady Christensen is still not activated while the team works out roster spots, and the interior depth is solid.

title: Zac Taylor Previews Week 7 Against Ravens | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Bengals look largely healthy for Baltimore: Dugger is progressing, Tee Higgins is available and Colbie Young could return to the rotation, while Chase Brown got praise for his pass protection against a blitz-heavy Ravens defense.
summary: Zac Taylor said the team is in good shape and trending the right way. Kyle Dugger was the one player he named, saying he is making good progress this week. On Colbie Young, Taylor did not commit to a specific role if he is cleared. He said the team keeps carving out roles for everyone who is healthy, and he praised Young as an improving, physical player who runs hard after the catch and can be a threat in the passing game. He called Tee Higgins a major weapon outside and noted that Higgins has made big plays against Baltimore even though he has missed some of those games. Most of the session was about the Ravens. Taylor said they have evolved since the Wink Martindale days, called a turnover win critical in a division game, and said the team will prepare all week for Lamar Jackson even though Tyler Huntley could play. He called Kyle Hamilton the most underrated player in football because of how many positions he plays and how often he blitzes. Taylor said the Bengals' backs are fearless in pass protection, and he singled out Chase Brown for how well he uses leverage and his hands. He also said a player still on IR with a hand injury, called 'Yoshi' in the question, is progressing but still has time left on IR. Taylor praised the pass rush and the Seattle free agent signing (apparently Boye Mafe) for his versatility and willingness to set the edge, and spent the end of the session praising Ted Karras's character.

Taylor called the division always strong and said no win in it ever feels easy. He was not surprised that every team is above .500, and he called this a big road game.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference : October 21st, 2026

He blamed the offense as a whole for inconsistent throwing, including protection calls, the quarterback and the players, and for a quiet first half last week. He expects more production from the top pass-catchers (Fannin, Denzel Boston, KC Concepcion) as the offense strings drives together, and he said Jerry Jeudy has come up big lately. He also praised the defense for ranking second in sacks without Myles Garrett, crediting the coaches for keeping the staff together and the players for embracing the scheme.

title: HC Sean Payton on facing the Cardinals’ defense: ‘We’re going to have to have the right answers'
headline: Payton owns the offense's struggles ahead of a pressure-heavy Arizona defense; Jonah Coleman may return, and Jonah Elliss's injury is not season-ending.
summary: Payton framed Week 7 around Arizona's pressure defense, which he said bothered the Rams and forced turnovers. He said Denver needs "the right answers" on third down and in play design, and he put the onus on himself and the staff to find more open throws, which he tied to Bo Nix's play. He called the offense a work in progress, with a good first half last week and a much weaker second half. He also said the run game still needs work after the last couple of weeks. On the injury front, he was optimistic about Jonah Elliss, saying the injury is not season-ending with details due later in the week. He was non-committal on Jonah Coleman's potential return, calling the running back room deep and talented and saying the team will see how the week goes. He praised Taylor Rapp's first snaps after joining the team, citing his football IQ and clean transition. On Arizona, he singled out tight end Trey McBride as their best weapon, compared him to Brock Bowers, and noted that McBride and Marvin Harrison Jr. produce heavily in the passing game. He also said Denver's pressure and turnovers were huge in last Thursday's win. A separate early answer about a player coming back under league protocol, with a "pitch count" and acclimation this week, never made clear who he meant.

Asked about veterans starting slowly, Payton said coaches look at themselves and the plan first to become more efficient. He did not single out any individual player.

title: Matt LaFleur on playing in Detroit: 'It's always a challenge'
headline: Josh Jacobs is back at practice after a stretch away from the team, but LaFleur would only say 'we'll work through it' on whether he plays Sunday at Detroit. With Jayden Reed out, Savion Williams is the lead candidate for Reed's motion and slot work, though LaFleur described it as a committee.
summary: LaFleur said Wednesday's practice was mostly a jog-through because the team is coming off a Sunday night game and he is watching the workload ahead. Josh Jacobs was back at practice and could join walk-throughs and team work for the first time. LaFleur said he has a good feel for Jacobs' conditioning because Jacobs has been working with the strength staff, but he was noncommittal on whether two full practices are enough for Jacobs to play Sunday. Asked about Jayden Reed's role, he said Savion Williams adds the pre-snap motion and slot element, and he also has confidence in Bo Melton, J. Michael Sturdivant and Skyy Moore to do some of it. He prefers having multiple players who can do those things in case of injury, and he treats it as a game-by-game decision. On Jacobs and the allegations against him, LaFleur said he believes Jacobs is remorseful and a good person, and that he believes in second chances. On the offense, he said the run game has not been as effective, but Green Bay remains committed to it after the week-three approach of throwing on every play did not work. He said the team has added a few more minutes of individual fundamentals time and does not want to overreact to drops. He called Detroit an explosive, well-coached team, praised Jahmyr Gibbs' ability to break tackles, and praised Jared Goff for playing at an MVP level without an interception.

injuries.detail: LaFleur's comments about replacing Reed's motion and slot usage imply Reed is out, but he did not give a status or a timeline.

headline: LB Drake Thomas is out of Wednesday's practice, and FB Brady Russell could see more two-back (21 personnel) snaps. Seattle plans to stay with wide zone against a Chiefs team led by ex-Seahawk Kenneth Walker.

He said Seattle's screen-game problems come from a couple of big plays and are a team-wide responsibility, not one player's. On offense, he said Seattle will run wide zone against everyone and mix in other run concepts depending on personnel and the opponent. The wide zone has been a bit more variable than he'd like. He called the offensive line's effort and attitude good but wants more decisiveness this week, and he said starting fast comes from decisiveness and alignment. He confirmed Drake Thomas won't practice Wednesday and gave no further detail. He made a passing comparison between Mahomes' recovery timetable and Zach Charbonnet's, with no update on Charbonnet's status. On run defense, he stressed fundamentals, team tackling and leverage, and said the defensive line sets the tone from the split-safety structure.

title: Shanahan Talks Offense’s Second-Half Struggles, Previews Falcons

title: Todd Bowles on Baker Mayfield’s Practice: Progress | Press Conference
headline: Baker Mayfield returned to practice with a glove on his injured thumb and looked effective. Bowles will decide on the Week 7 starter after Friday's practice, so Mayfield is a watch-list QB with Jalon Daniels as the fallback.
summary: Bowles said Mayfield's thumb is coming along fine. He wore a glove for the whole practice, got loose as the session went on, and looked effective. Bowles called it encouraging but said he needs to see how the thumb responds after a day of gripping the ball, and he will decide after Friday's practice. Mayfield and Jalon Daniels split the work, with each getting mental reps and only some physical reps. Bowles said both know the game plan and are ready to play. Bowles stressed that the team needs to settle on a quarterback early for planning purposes. He said a thumb is easier to gauge than Mayfield's earlier shoulder and bruise issues, because it shows in his throwing and snaps under center. He said Antoine Winfield Jr. was in a non-contact jersey and must practice without it before he can return, so his status is unclear this week. Bowles admitted Chris Godwin has been used just "okay" and the offense needs to get him open more. He also said he wants to free up Calijah Kancey, who has few sacks despite being in the backfield, and he noted that downfield throws have been hurt by holding penalties and sacks. He praised the Panthers' offense, Bryce Young and play-caller Brad.
